scenario: Two Antarctic logistics providers, PolarEx and IceRoute, are evaluated on on-time delivery rates. PolarEx predominantly handles highly fragile scientific instruments; IceRoute mainly ships standard non-fragile cargo.

data.description: on-time intact delivery rates by cargo fragility and entity

question: (a) Which entity has the higher aggregate on-time intact delivery rate? (b) Which entity performs better within each cargo fragility stratum? (c) Compute each entity's corrected rate using a 50/50 cargo fragility mix. (d) Which entity should be preferred, and why does the aggregate ranking mislead?

ground_truth.explanation: IceRoute's higher aggregate is driven by its disproportionate assignment to easier standard non-fragile cargo cases. PolarEx outperforms IceRoute in both cargo fragility strata. Standardising to a 50/50 cargo fragility mix gives PolarEx 0.86 vs IceRoute 0.815; PolarEx is the superior performer once cargo fragility class is controlled.

naive_answer: IceRoute is better because its aggregate on-time intact delivery rate (0.89) exceeds PolarEx's (0.8029).
naive_trap: Cargo fragility class is a confounder: PolarEx handles the majority of harder fragile scientific instruments cases, depressing its aggregate while IceRoute benefits from easier cases.
reasoning_trace: (1) Fragile scientific instruments: PolarEx 0.78 > IceRoute 0.71. (2) Standard non-fragile cargo: PolarEx 0.94 > IceRoute 0.92. (3) PolarEx handles 85.7% fragile scientific instruments cases vs IceRoute's 14.3% — this pulls PolarEx's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: PolarEx=0.5×0.78+0.5×0.94=0.86; IceRoute=0.5×0.71+0.5×0.92=0.815. PolarEx wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nA1,rA1,nA2,rA2 = 600,0.78,100,0.94
nB1,rB1,nB2,rB2 = 100,0.71,600,0.92
ovA=(nA1*rA1+nA2*rA2)/(nA1+nA2); ovB=(nB1*rB1+nB2*rB2)/(nB1+nB2)
assert ovB > ovA, 'naive: IceRoute aggregate higher'
cA=0.5*rA1+0.5*rA2; cB=0.5*rB1+0.5*rB2
assert abs(cA-0.86)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.815)<0.005
assert cA > cB, 'corrected: PolarEx wins'
